summary: Helmut Rix was a scholar in linguistics and indology who studied at the University of Würzburg (~1950–1956). He held posts at the University of Regensburg (~1968–1978) and the University of Freiburg (~1978–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a tibetology and buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner (~1975–1981). He served as a professor at the University of Vienna (~1982–2019) and was a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University (~2011–2012).

Helmuth von Glasenapp worked in indology, religious studies, and buddhist studies, studying under Hermann Jacobi, Wanczura, and at Bonn and Berlin. He taught at Bonn and Berlin (1918–1929) and held chairs at Königsberg (1929–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

Hendrik Kern worked in indology, buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Utrecht University (~1850–1853), Leiden University (~1853–1855), and under Albrecht Weber (1855–1856), later serving as professor at Leiden University (1865–1903).

Heng Sure is a scholar of buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD ~1998–2003) under Ronald Y. Nakasone, Edmond Yee, Raoul Birnbaum, and teacher Hsuan Hua (~1976–1995).
Henk Blezer is a scholar of tibetology and buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University from ~1988 to 1997 and held a post there in ~1997.

Henk Bodewitz specialized in indology and linguistics, completing his PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1963–1973). He served as dean of arts at Utrecht (1980–1982) and as a professor at Leiden University (1992–2002).
Henri Gaidoz was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber in 1865.

Henri Maspero specialized in sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, studying at Lycée Montaigne, Lycée Louis-le-Grand, and ENLOV. He held posts at the EFEO (1911–1914), Collège de France (1920–1945), and Maison Franco-Japonaise (1928–1930).

Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at Liège, Frederick William University Berlin, Leipzig, Paris, EPHE, and Ghent. He held academic posts at the University of Liège (~1885–1886) and Ghent University (1886–1930).
Henrik Samuel Nyberg worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University in 1908 and held a post there from ~1919 to 1956.
Henrik Zilliacus was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1926–1936) and later held a post there (~1944–1974).

Henry Chung-hung Shiu works in buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto (~1999–2006) and studied under Shek-wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, Julia Ching, Willard Gurdon Oxtoby, and Wing-cheuk Chan.

Henry Clarke Warren specialized in buddhist studies and indology. He studied at Harvard University (B.A. ~1875–1879), Johns Hopkins University (1879), and under Charles Rockwell Lanman (1879), and founded the Harvard Oriental Series.

Henry George Keene was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and indological studies. He held posts at the East India Company (~1798–1811) and the East India Company College (~1824–1834) as Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature.

Henry Herbert Dodwell worked in history, archaeology, and indology, after studying at Lord Williams's School and St John's College (~1895–1899). He served in the Indian Educational Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History of India at SOAS (~1922–1946).

Henry Pitts Forster was an indology and linguistics scholar. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1783–1815) and held the post of Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata (~1803–1815).
Henry Sullivan Jarrett was an indology and history/archaeology scholar. He held a post as Secretary and Member at the Board of Examiners, Calcutta (~1870–1892).

Henry T. Wright is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Michigan (~1960–1964) and University of Chicago (~1964–1967). He held posts at the University of Michigan (~1967) and the Santa Fe Institute.

Henry Thomas Colebrooke was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati. He held posts in the Bengal Civil Service, Fort William College (1782–1814), and Sadar Diwani Adalat, and served as Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (1823–1837).
